test_title: RRB Group D Official Paper (Held On: 11 Dec, 2025 Shift 2)
subject: general
question:
Simplify :

 (1-sec x)/(csc x · cot x)
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Put x = 60° in the expression: (1 − sec 60°) / (csc 60° × cot 60°)

⇒ (1 − 2) / (2/√3 × 1/√3) = −1 / (2/3) = −3/2

Check Option C: (cos 60° − 1) tan² 60° = (1/2 − 1) × (√3)² = (−1/2) × 3 = −3/2

Since the values match, Option C is the correct simplification.

**∴ The correct option is C.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Given: Expression = (1 − sec x) / (csc x × cot x)

Formula Used: sec x = 1/cos x, csc x = 1/sin x, cot x = cos x / sin x, tan x = sin x / cos x

⇒ (1 − 1/cos x) / [(1/sin x) × (cos x / sin x)]

⇒ [(cos x − 1) / cos x] / [cos x / sin² x]

⇒ [(cos x − 1) / cos x] × [sin² x / cos x]

⇒ (cos x − 1) × [sin² x / cos² x]

⇒ (cos x − 1) tan² x

**∴ The correct option is C.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Pythagorean Identities

sin²x + cos²x = 1, 1 + tan²x = sec²x, and 1 + cot²x = csc²x.

Reciprocal Identities

sec x = 1/cos x, csc x = 1/sin x, and cot x = 1/tan x.

Quotient Identities

tan x = sin x / cos x and cot x = cos x / sin x.
